Goal for this file:

- Your hypotheses.
- The variables you plan to use.
- Code to create a tidy dataset.
- Code to create a codebook.


1. My Hypotheses

H1 One categorical IV – continuous DV prediction

Political beliefs (cat = left to right in 5 steps) 
effect on 
Physical attractiveness (scale = 11 point rating) 

H2 One continuous-continuous prediction

Importance of looking attractive (Attract_importance_1, scale 1-9)
positive effect on
Daily time spent enhancing appearance  (composite variable, sum of 8 scales)



```{r packages}

# load packages

library(codebook)
library(dplyr)

```

## 1. Create subset

```{r data}

#load data/raw/data_doctored.csv
raw <- read.csv("data/lab02_files/data_doctored.csv")

summary(raw)

# Attract_importance_1


#make data with ID, cot_politics, self_physatt, Time_A_makeup_1, Time_A_hyg_1, Time_A_cosm_1, Time_A_exercise_1, Time_A_hair_1, Time_A_dress_1, Time_A_diet_1, Time_A_other_1


# create subset
# manually choose columns, check colnames or str
data <- raw[,c("ResponseId", "Attract_importance_1", "cot_politics", "self_physatt",
               "Time_A_makeup_1","Time_A_hyg_1","Time_A_cosm_1",
               "Time_A_exercise_1", "Time_A_hair_1","Time_A_dress_1",
               "Time_A_diet_1", "Time_A_other_1")]


# rename columns, because capitalized letters in dataframes suck
data <- data %>% 
  rename(
    id = ResponseId,
    attract_importance_1 = Attract_importance_1,
    cot_politics = cot_politics,
    self_physatt = self_physatt, 
    time_a_makeup_1 = Time_A_makeup_1,
    time_a_hyg_1 = Time_A_hyg_1,
    time_a_cosm_1 = Time_A_cosm_1,
    time_a_exercise_1 = Time_A_exercise_1,
    time_a_hair_1 = Time_A_hair_1, 
    time_a_dress_1 = Time_A_dress_1,
    time_a_diet_1 = Time_A_diet_1,
    time_a_other_1 = Time_A_other_1
  )

# check
dim(data)
str(data)
summary(data)



```
## 2. Check participant IDs

```{r check ID}

#look for na, blank, duplicates
summary(data$id)
# we have 1 duplicate, 1 NA, 0 blanks


#inspect records with missing or blank IDs
missingID <- which(is.na(data$id))

#remove the known empty record with no ID, then check the row count
#remove NA
data <- data[!is.na(data$id),]

#check again
missingID <- which(is.na(data$id))
data[missingID,]
```

## 3. recode Political beliefs category variable

```{r political beliefs category recode}

# codebook: "1=Far left; 2=Center left; 3=Center; 4=Center right; 5=Far right."


#turn cot_politics into a factor with labels 1=Far left; 2=Center left; 3=Center; 4=Center right; 5=Far right.

table(data$cot_politics, useNA="ifany")

data$cot_politics <- factor(data$cot_politics,
                         levels = c(1:5),
                         labels = c("far_left", "center_left", "center", "center_right", "far_right"))

```

## 6. Daily time spent enhancing appearance  (composite variable, sum of 8 scales)

```{r app_enh}
#group all 8 appearance enhancing (app_enh) time variables

colnames(data)
              
summary(data$time_a_makeup_1)
summary(data$time_a_hyg_1)
summary(data$time_a_cosm_1)
summary(data$time_a_exercise_1)
summary(data$time_a_hair_1)
summary(data$time_a_dress_1)
summary(data$time_a_diet_1)
summary(data$time_a_diet_1)
# all looks good
               
# create a vector with names of columns
app_enh_vars <- c("time_a_makeup_1","time_a_hyg_1","time_a_cosm_1",
                  "time_a_exercise_1", "time_a_hair_1","time_a_dress_1",
                  "time_a_diet_1", "time_a_diet_1")


#see summary of variables
# give that vector to df and ask for summary of those values
summary(data[,app_enh_vars])
# alternative
summary(data[,4:11])

#count NAs
colSums(is.na(data[,app_enh_vars]))
# alternative
colSums(is.na(data[,4:11]))

# calculate total score; leave the total NA if any item is missing
# create new column called app_enh_total
data$app_enh_total <- rowSums(data[app_enh_vars], na.rm=F)

# if I make NAs in my individual variables make the total = NA, i lose a LOT of data, see below:
# count NA values
sum(is.na(data$app_enh_total))
# 109540
# count NOT NA values 
sum(!is.na(data$app_enh_total))
# 7753

# since my composite score, I choose to calculate with na.rm=T - leaving my sum scores intact, even if there are NAs in the variables.
# We are counting sum of time here, and if someone does not report for a single time scale, I still want to consider the sum time.
# This of course would be up for debate on how to handle this.
# In this case I choose to continue with, na.rm=T and more data I can work with.

data$app_enh_total <- rowSums(data[app_enh_vars], na.rm=T)
# count NA values
sum(is.na(data$app_enh_total))
# 0
# count NOT NA values 
sum(!is.na(data$app_enh_total))
# 117293

# but now I have 0 NAs, even though some IDs have not given answers, making their answer total sum 0 - which is technically also wrong.
# so:

# use deplyr package
# check if every variable is NA, if yes, return NA in app_enh_total - if no, return  sum
data <- data %>%
  mutate(
    app_enh_total = if_else(
      rowSums(!is.na(pick(all_of(app_enh_vars)))) == 0,
      NA_real_,
      rowSums(pick(all_of(app_enh_vars)), na.rm = TRUE)
    )
  )
# count NA values
sum(is.na(data$app_enh_total))
# 23382
# count NOT NA values 
sum(!is.na(data$app_enh_total))
# 93911

# Now we have kept most of our data.

summary(data$app_enh_total)
hist(data$app_enh_total)

colnames(data)



```

## 7. create h1 dataframe

H1 One categorical IV – continuous DV prediction

Political beliefs (cat = left to right in 5 steps) 
effect on 
Physical attractiveness (scale = 11 point rating) 

```{r h1 data frame}

# make h1_data with "id", "cot_politics", "self_physatt"


# code to remove all rows with NAs
h1_data <- na.omit(data[c("id", "cot_politics", "self_physatt")])


# plot
boxplot(self_physatt ~ cot_politics, data = h1_data)

```


## 8. create h2 dataframe

H2 One continuous-continuous prediction

Importance of looking attractive (Attract_importance_1, scale 1-9)
positive effect on
Daily time spent enhancing appearance  (composite variable, sum of 8 scales)

```{r h2 data frame}

# code to remove all rows with NAs
h2_data <- na.omit(data[c("id", "attract_importance_1", "app_enh_total")])



# plot
boxplot(app_enh_total ~ attract_importance_1, data = h2_data)

```

## 10. Add labels and generate codebooks

The descriptions come from the original codebook and our scoring decisions.
`compact_codebook()` adds summaries from the actual data. Knit the Rmd to
display the formatted codebooks.

```{r}
#add a description to each h1_data column, in column order
#include the source codes, meaning, and units
var_label(h1_data) <- c(
  "id: Unique participant ID",
  "cot_politics: self-reported political belief, original codes 1=Far left; 2=Center left; 3=Center; 4=Center right; 5=Far right ; now stored as a factor",
  "self_physatt: Self-rating of physical attractiveness: scale from 1 - 11 (1=Very low, 6=Average, 11=Very high)"
)

#add a description to each h2_data column, in column order
#include response anchors and the commitment scoring rule
var_label(h2_data) <- c(
  "id: Unique participant ID",
  "attract_importance_1: Self reported importance of own attractivness: scale from 1-9 (1 - not at all important - 9 - extremely important)",
  "app_enh_total - Daily time spent enhancing appearance (in minutes): Composite score, sum of time_a_makeup_1,time_a_hyg_1,time_a_cosm_1, time_a_exercise_1, time_a_hair_1,time_a_dress_1, time_a_diet_1, time_a_diet_1; each individual variable having a max. value of 360 minutes."
)
```

H1 includes participants with an ID, a valid political belief category, and a score on for self rating of physical attractiveness from 1 -11. Factor level numbers in the generated table are internal R positions, not the original survey codes.

```{r h1_codebook}
#generate the h1Data codebook
compact_codebook(h1_data)

```

H2 includes participants with an ID,  Self reported importance of own attractivness: scale from 1-9, and Daily time spent enhancing appearance (in minutes).

```{r h2_codebook}
#generate the h2Data codebook
compact_codebook(h2_data)
```

## 11. Save the final tables

```{r save}
#create data/processed_data if needed
dir.create("data/processed_data",recursive=T,showWarnings=F)

#save h1Data and h2Data without an extra row-number column
write.csv(h1_data,"data/processed_data/practice_h1.csv",row.names=F)
write.csv(h2_data,"data/processed_data/practice_h2.csv",row.names=F)

#read the files back and confirm their dimensions
h1_saved <- read.csv("data/processed_data/practice_h1.csv")
h2_saved <- read.csv("data/processed_data/practice_h2.csv")
dim(h1_saved)
dim(h2_saved)
```
